featured_reviews.name: Jayashri Devadhar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having heard reviews about this tiny but interesting joint at Charni Road serving Locho, we decided to go there a few days ago. Needless to say, it was extremely tiny with seating for just 5 people at max.

The menu showed pizzas, wraps, fries and a few other stuff too along with a wide variety of Locho but we decided to go with what the place is known for. Everything in the menu, we were told, could be made Jain, except for what was expressly named as containing garlic. We tried the basic oil Locho and butter garlic Locho, both of which were good and quite distinct in taste. I would give the butter locho a slightly upper hand for its flavours and along with the Sev on top and chopped onion and green chutney served alongside, it tasted delicious. Would surely come back again for it when Locho cravings strike back!

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place is just outside the Charni road station East, you can see this place from the skywalk itself. On weekends you will find a really good young and family crowd at the same time you will experience a lot of people here. This place (The whole khau gali) only serves veg and you will get food in the price range of Rs. 40 to Rs. 200-250. It's a really nice place if you want to explore the food and don't want to be too harsh on your pocket as well. The place serves chaat, veg tikka, Franky, rolls, pasta, pizza, sandwiches, juice and shakes etc

The things which I tried and want you to experience are:

1. Paani Puri - So we started with chaat and we chose to try it from the shop so the puri which they served was of rawa so I will recommend you to try the chaat from the stall which is on the street and serves different types of paani.

2. Chinese bhel - This we tried from the street side stall but I felt this could have been better as I did not find that tangy taste and I have tried better at many places. Schezwan was not that spicy and I felt that something was missing.

3. Tandoor paneer pizza - So I tried it from the shop that was just next to the paani Puri shop. The pizza was of the thin crust base and I felt it was okayish. You can better try it from the pasta stall the one on the street.

4. Veg tikka : So at this tikka place you can get potatoes, tomatoes, mushroom and Shimla mirch tikka. I recommend you to try this for just Rs. 40 plate and you can experience good food here. The tikka is served with onion and green chutney. ❤️ Recommended

5. Pasta - We tried pink sauce penne pasta. It was definitely worth it. Tangy taste, good quantity and range is of 70-200 you shall visit this stall. You can choose your own pasta and the sauce.

After this we took a break as we wanted to explore more but our stomach started saying no, so we took one jaljeera soda from the stall just next to the tikka stall and went for a walk to see some nearby places. Then we came back with the bang. After the break we tried

6. Mysore dosa - So frankly speaking I like dosa crunchy but the one which they served was soggy and I feel that you can skip the dosa part here or at least the Mysore dosa you can skip. You can try some other better dosas.

7. Bellbottom shake : Last but not the least I'll definitely recommend you to try this. With the toppings of dry fruit, one scoop of vanilla, blue berry and thick shake of strawberry and blue berry. You will love it. I wanted to try this and I did not regret it.

You can also find Franky, sandwiches and other stalls. I only tried all this but there is much more variety. For Western line you just need to take a slow train and get down at Charni road station. Whereas for the central and harbour line people you need to get down at dadar and then you can take the churchgate slow train and get down at Charni road station.

We went to Flavors at Bay near Hotel Hira mainly because it was convenient for us. Unfortunately, the food was a big disappointment.

I understand that it’s a vegetarian restaurant and spices are an important part of Indian cooking, but spices should complement the meal — not completely overpower it. Everything we ordered tasted like it was just packed with masala and nothing else.

We ordered momos, and they were honestly the worst part of the meal. They didn’t taste like real momos at all. Instead of a proper filling, it felt like a dough ball stuffed with pure spices. The taste matched how it looked — just overwhelming masala with no balance. Coming from a Nepali background where we eat momos often, this was really disappointing.

The biryani was the same story. It was mostly spice with very little flavor or balance beyond that.

The service itself was good and the staff were polite. The location was convenient for us as well. However, the restaurant felt quite empty and overall the food experience was not good. Unfortunately, the heavy spices even gave us heartburn afterwards.

We really wanted to enjoy the meal, but it ended up being a very disappointing experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sankalp P
featured_reviews.review_text:
CP Tank Pasta – A Street Food Worth Drooling Over

If you’re looking for a pasta that makes you crave more, CP Tank Pasta is where it’s at. It’s the kind of street food that keeps you coming back for more, and I totally get why!

The Pasta: 5/5

I ordered the Pink Sauce Pasta, and wow, it was one of the best decisions I’ve made. The sauce was creamy, rich, and balanced – not too heavy but just enough to coat every strand of pasta perfectly. The texture of the pasta itself was spot-on, soft yet with a bite, and cooked just right. The best part? The sauce was packed with flavor – tangy, slightly sweet, and full of depth. It’s the kind of pasta that you don’t want to stop eating.

The vegetables they added were a nice touch. There were fancy bits of bell peppers, olives, and mushrooms sprinkled in, giving it a fresh crunch and extra layers of flavor. These veggies weren't overwhelming but complimented the sauce and pasta perfectly. Honestly, it felt like the rain outside was the perfect backdrop for this warm, comforting plate of pasta.

Portion & Price: 5/5

The portion was generous for the price. At just ₹200, I was pleasantly surprised by how much they give you. It’s filling without being overstuffed, so you get a satisfying meal without breaking the bank. For street food, it’s really a steal!

The Vibe: 4/5

This isn’t a sit-down, fancy restaurant vibe—it’s street food done right. Whether you're standing at a cart or sitting at a tiny bench, you’re there for the food, and that’s what matters. It’s casual and quick, which is exactly what you want when you're craving something delicious to snack on during a rainy day.

Final Thoughts: 5/5

If you love pasta, CP Tank Pasta is a must-try. It’s the kind of street food that will make you crave it on repeat. The combination of the perfect pink sauce, the right veggies, and the incredible price makes this an easy favorite. It’s warm, flavorful, and ideal for those cozy rainy days when you're looking out your window with a plate of pasta in hand. Definitely going to go back – no doubt about it!

A Highly Disappointing Maharashtrian Food
Overall Rating: 3/10 (Based primarily on food Taste and facilities)
My recent visit to Vinay in Girgaon was a profound disappointment, particularly for anyone seeking authentic, high-quality Maharashtrian snacks. The experience was marred by poor execution of core dishes and subpar facilities, resulting in one of the worst quick-service dining experiences I've had in a while.
The Food Verdict
The most critical failure of the visit was the Misal Pav.
• Misal Pav: 1/10
This was, quite frankly, one of the worst Misal Pavs I have ever encountered. It lacked the characteristic spice, texture, and authentic flavor profile that defines this Maharashtrian staple. It was sweet 😂. If Misal is your purpose for visiting, please look elsewhere.
• Other Dishes: 3/10 (Okish)
We also sampled the Sabudana Wada, Vatana Pattice, and Veg Biryani. While these items were merely "okish," they still scored a very low 3 out of 10. They lacked freshness, or any distinguishing quality to warrant a recommendation or even a second thought.
Ambiance and Facilities
On a positive note, the restaurant offers good sitting options, including both AC and Non-AC sections, which is a rare plus point in this category.
However, the facility challenges are severe:
• Parking: There is no dedicated parking available, which can be a significant hassle in the congested Girgaon area.
• Toilets: The washroom facilities were, without exaggeration, the worst. This is a major area needing immediate attention and upkeep.
Final Recommendation
If your goal is to experience good, authentic, and delicious Maharashtrian cuisine, do not visit Vinay. You will be better served by traveling a little further to established names.
Alternative Recommendations for Authentic Maharashtrian Food:
• Misal Pav: For a truly great Misal, visit Mamledar Misal (Thane).
• General Maharashtrian Cuisine: For excellent, reliable snacks and meals, Prakash Shuddh Upahar Kendra (Dadar) remains a gold standard.

name: Juice Time
description:
Juice Time – Pure Vegetarian & Jain Restaurant | Opera House, Mumbai

For 14 years, Juice Time has proudly served 100% pure vegetarian and Jain food, prepared with love, purity, and flavor. Known for its wide range of freshly made juices, rolls, sandwiches, pasta, pizzas, Chinese, Asian, Oriental, Italian, Mexican, sizzlers, pav bhaji, and desserts, Juice Time is your go-to spot for delicious vegetarian meals.

Whether you’re craving a wholesome snack or a full meal, enjoy a fresh, hygienic, and flavor-packed dining experience — because at Juice Time, we’re proudly vegetarian and always will be.

featured_reviews.name: Mansee Nisar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is one of the sobos best veg and jain restaurant. My jain friends visit this restaurant too often and they love the food out here. Even i came here for the 3rd time in a row. As soon as I came to know they introduced some new items on the menu, I went there to try it .
Some of their regulars are  bamboo rice and various varieties of rolls .
Apart from these we tried their cheesy pao bhaji, cheese burst pizza which melted our hearts , hummus platter , and spicy panner burger . We loved everything.
Drinks were also on point eena meena deeka which was a combination drink .
It was really good to see that they keep on introducing new items on the menu . Will keep visiting for such more often .

featured_reviews.name: DISHA HARAN
featured_reviews.review_text: “Juice Time is truly a hidden gem in South Mumbai for pure veg & Jain food lovers! 🌟 Open till late night, the menu has so much variety with fresh flavors, quick service, and great quality. Perfect spot for family dinners, midnight cravings, and even small celebrations with their spacious party area. Highly recommended for anyone looking for tasty vegetarian food with a great vibe! 💚”

featured_reviews.name: Dhananjay Purohit
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had an absolutely terrible experience at Juice Time. The customer service was beyond disappointing — the staff were rude, inattentive, and acted like they were doing me a favor by even acknowledging my order. There was zero professionalism and no basic courtesy.

The food was just as bad. What I received was poorly prepared, tasted awful, and honestly felt unhygienic. It’s shocking how low the quality was, especially considering how simple the menu is.

What made it worse was the overall attitude — no accountability, no apology, and no effort to improve the situation. It’s one thing to serve bad food, but combining that with such disgusting service makes it a place I would strongly advise everyone to avoid.

Definitely one of the worst experiences I’ve had. Never ordering from here again.

featured_reviews.name: The Wandering Veggie
featured_reviews.review_text:
We ordered Falafel Shawarma 🥙, Pasta pe Pasta and Firangi (Peru+Strawberry) Juice 🍹

The Falafel Shawarma  was lovely, hummus, pickled beetroot, other veggies, falafels, everything was perfect.

The Firangi juice had more peru(guava) taste than strawberry, but was fresh and not too sugary. Will definitely try other curious combos the next time.

Pasta pe Pasta was a combination of macaroni in cheesy sauce and speghetti in red sauce, taste was pretty good, the breads served with it were a little dry.

Staff was very nice and let us use the group seating area which could easily accommodate 9-10 people although we were just 2. The ambience is pretty good.

If you advance book through Zomato Gold Dining option and then pay through Zomato Gold, you get flat 15% off on total bill which is a steal deal.
